lines.text: So. The valley sends swords instead of grain. I expected it.
Come, then. My grandchildren are watching, and they are hungry.
You lock your grain and call us thieves. Now you come to finish it.
Old, yes. Soft, no.
Hah. The hill is crooked. Like your mayor.
Forty winters I have bled for this clan. Your turn.
Go down to the river. Tell it Skarrow sent you.
Up, little one. Up. Ah. No.
Not yet. The little ones have not eaten.
I have buried better than you. I will not be buried by you.
Go home. Tell them the bridge stays ours until the grain comes.
Whatever you think of me, feed the little ones. Feed them.
Valley people. Walking. Not running at me with spears. This is new.
Forty winters I have held this clan. Do not ask me if I can hold it one more.
Sit. You are guests now, which is worse than enemies. Guests we have to feed.
Valley people. Walking. Not running at me with spears. This is new.
You lock your grain and call us thieves. Sit. We will talk about who stole what.
Two-day bread. From the innkeeper, yes? The one who feeds anybody.
Small kindness. Small stomachs. It is not nothing.
Ha! Somebody's mother taught you properly. You say my name like you have been scolded with it.
Then you know a hill word the valley does not have. It means a debt that both sides pretend is a gift.
Then you saw. My little ones were down on the bank, digging roots. Your people shot at them.
We took the bridge after. Not before. Tell your captain that, if she will hear it.
Here is the bargain, and it is a short one. Your town eats. My clan eats. The bridge goes back to being a bridge.
Not coin. Coin does not boil. A share of the grain your mayor keeps behind his locks. Every week, until the thaw.
Half now, half at the thaw. You bargain like a hill grandmother. I will take it, and I will watch you.
Half? My children do not eat half. All of it, every week, or go home and fetch your captain.
But you climbed the hill. So. Sit down again, and agree with me.
Most of them. Some of the young ones belong to my grandson now, in their hearts. Vorga. He left us to take instead of ask.
His friends will not like a truce. If they bare their teeth on the bridge, do not kill more of them than you must.
Forty winters I have held this clan. Do not ask me if I can hold it one more.
Then it is agreed. Tell your mayor the old mother will give back his bridge. Tell him she is counting the sacks.
I see you, valley people. You came with spears after all. I hoped. I am old enough to know better than hope.
Come, then. Every one of us you kill is one less mouth this winter. Your mayor will be so pleased.
Hm. Well fought. My grandson always said the valley would never share. I should have listened to him.
There was a song I meant to teach somebody. Too late now. It goes into the river with me.
Seven went up where the wall meets the sky. No. Not for you. Not for the ones with spears.
My grandson's friends. They would rather die on the stones than eat valley bread. Foolish children.
Do what you must. But I have buried enough of them this year. Leave me some to scold.
They will go to him. He will tell them they were brave. They were. Brave is cheap this winter.
Your captain thinks. Good. Tell her to think about the grain.
Sit. You are guests now, which is worse than enemies. Guests we have to feed.
When the bellies are full, the clan sings. Tonight I sing the old one, because my bones say I should.
The valley song. Seven went over, seven came home, they brought something heavy. Yes. Pretty.
Your song was made by the ones who came home. Ours was made by the ones who watched them come.
Hm. I thought you smelled wrong. Not bad. Only far. Like snow from the other side.
Then listen close. This song is about your side of the mountain, a little. Perhaps it is about you.
Seven went up where the wall meets the sky, seven with nothing, and hungry, and cold.
Seven came down when the snow was still falling, seven came down with their hands full of gold.
But nobody runs when they carry a fortune. Seven came down, and the seven came running.
That is the next verse. And the next verse is not for strangers.
You fed my children. That makes you something. Not family. Not yet. Come back when you are.
You ask well. So, a crumb. In the old song the gold is not gold. We sing gold because it rhymes, and the true word is sad.
The rest when you are family. Not before. Now eat. You are too thin for valley people.
You fed my children, valley people. So I give you what I do not give to strangers. Not all of it. The last verse stays with the clan.
Seven went over the Greywall in the long winters, and seven came back with fire. They came back running.
The song says the fire had a home on the far side of the mountains. The seven took it. It was not theirs to take.
Your Wardens sang that it was given. We never warmed our hands at it, so we never forgot. It was stolen.
My grandson Vorga holds the bridge you need. He is a fool and a thief, and he is mine.
Do not kill him, if you can help it. Beat him if you must. Then send him home to me.
Warm again. Good for the children. But watch. In ten winters you valley folk will forget you owe us grain.
We never used your fire, so we will remember for you. Somebody has to sing it.
Cold again, like the old songs. Now you valley folk learn what we know. Sit. We will teach you how to winter.
Neighbours. That is your word for people you shout at and still feed. Good. We will be neighbours.
You lock your grain and call us thieves. Come, then, valley folk. Take the bridge from an old woman.
They are in the water! Shoot them while they wade, children!
Forty winters I have buried grandchildren. I will not bury more for you. Sing with me!
